**Turn Me On** – the song that appears on Norah Jones’s *Feelin’ the Same Way* (segment of *Come Away with Me*) – was written by **John D. Loudermilk**.  
- The original 1961 version was first recorded by Mark Dinning, but the composition is credited to Loudermilk.  
- Norah Jones covered the tune for her debut album and released it as a single in 2003.

**Source**

"**Turn Me On**" is a song by [John D. Loudermilk] that was first recorded and released by [Mark Dinning] in 1961 as the [B-side] to his single "Lonely Island". Other notable versions are by Nellie Rutherford and [Nina Simone].[[5]]#cite_note-5)[Norah Jones] released her version as the last single from her debut album _[Come Away with Me]_ on May 12, 2003. The song was also performed by [Shelby Dressel] during her _[American Idol]_ audition.[[6]]#cite_note-6)

## Influence

[[edit]&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Influence")]

Musicologist [Joe Hickerson] suggested that "Turn Me On" influenced the composition of Leonard Cohen's 1969 song "[Bird on the Wire]".[[7]]#cite_note-7)

## Norah Jones version

[[edit]&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Norah Jones version")]

Jones's cover was the seventh track on her debut album. This version also appeared in the soundtrack of the movie _[Love Actually]_.
